owner: Migration Assessment Team (placeholder role — to be assigned by governance)

changelog.author: ReframeX Phase 5
changelog.summary: Initial ruleset covering all 8 domains across complexity, confidence, and readiness.

rules.description: COBOL program with high paragraph count indicates complex control flow
rules.detection_condition: component_type == 'MODULE' and technology == 'COBOL' and detected_properties.paragraph_count present and detected_properties.paragraph_count > 10
rules.explanation: A COBOL program with more than 10 paragraphs suggests intricate control flow that increases migration effort.
rules.recommendation: Review the program's paragraph structure and identify opportunities for modular refactoring before migration.

rules.description: GOTO statements indicate unstructured control flow
rules.explanation: GOTO statements create unstructured control flow that is difficult to map to modern structured programming constructs.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all GOTO targets and rewrite them as structured PERFORM or IF/ELSE blocks during refactoring.

rules.description: ALTER statements indicate deprecated altered-GOTO pattern
rules.explanation: ALTER statements modify GOTO targets at runtime, making control flow non-deterministic and extremely hard to refactor.
rules.recommendation: Identify all ALTER-GOTO pairs and plan manual rewrite — there is no automated equivalent in modern languages.

rules.description: High PERFORM nesting depth indicates complex logic
rules.detection_condition: component_type == 'CONTROL_FLOW' and detected_properties.max_nesting_depth present and detected_properties.max_nesting_depth >= 3
rules.explanation: Deeply nested PERFORM structures complicate understanding and refactoring of business logic.
rules.recommendation: Flatten deeply nested PERFORM blocks into separate paragraphs or subroutines.

rules.description: Dynamic CALL to variable target indicates runtime-dependent program flow
rules.explanation: Dynamic CALLs resolve the target program at runtime, making it impossible to fully trace program flow statically.
rules.recommendation: Identify all possible values of the CALL variable through data flow analysis and document each target.

rules.description: Static CALLs increase program-to-program coupling
rules.explanation: Each static CALL adds a program-to-program dependency that must be migrated together.
rules.recommendation: Map all static CALL targets and ensure they are included in the migration scope.

rules.description: REDEFINES in working storage indicate overlapping data reinterpretation
rules.evidence_requirement: component evidence_refs with rule COBOL_WORKING_STORAGE or COBOL_FD_RECORD
rules.explanation: REDEFINES allows different data types to share the same memory, a pattern with no direct equivalent in most modern languages.
rules.recommendation: Document each REDEFINES usage and plan explicit conversion logic or union types in the target language.

rules.description: COMP-3 packed-decimal fields require special numeric handling
rules.evidence_requirement: component evidence_refs with rule COBOL_WORKING_STORAGE or COBOL_FD_RECORD
rules.explanation: Packed-decimal (COMP-3) is an EBCDIC-centric numeric format that requires explicit conversion logic.
rules.recommendation: Identify all COMP-3 fields and plan conversion to appropriate decimal types in the target platform.
rules.upgrade_guidance: COMP-3/packed-decimal is an EBCDIC-specific format. Most target platforms use native decimal types. Plan explicit byte-level conversion during data migration.

rules.description: Large OCCURS arrays indicate complex data structures
rules.detection_condition: component_type == 'DATA_STRUCTURE' and detected_properties.occurs_max present and detected_properties.occurs_max >= 50
rules.evidence_requirement: component evidence_refs with rule COBOL_WORKING_STORAGE or COBOL_FD_RECORD
rules.explanation: Large fixed-size OCCURS arrays may need to be converted to dynamic collections in modern platforms.
rules.recommendation: Evaluate whether fixed-size OCCURS arrays should become dynamic collections in the target platform.

rules.description: Copybook usage increases shared data structure coupling
rules.explanation: Copybooks are shared data definitions included in multiple programs, creating implicit coupling between all programs that use them.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all copybook usages and plan a shared data definition module in the target architecture.

rules.description: COPY with REPLACING indicates conditional data structure variation
rules.explanation: COPY REPLACING creates per-program variations of shared copybooks, adding complexity to data structure analysis.
rules.recommendation: Document each REPLACING variant and plan for parameterized or templated data definitions in the target.

rules.description: COMP binary fields require numeric format conversion
rules.evidence_requirement: component evidence_refs with rule COBOL_WORKING_STORAGE or COBOL_FD_RECORD
rules.explanation: COMP (binary) fields use platform-specific byte ordering and size that may differ in the target environment.
rules.recommendation: Verify byte ordering and field sizes for all COMP fields against the target platform.

rules.description: Embedded SQL statements indicate tight database coupling
rules.explanation: Embedded SQL tightly couples the program to a specific database schema and dialect, requiring careful extraction.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all embedded SQL statements and evaluate whether to use an ORM, stored procedures, or data access layer.

rules.description: DDL defines database schema structures
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with category SQL_DDL or SQL
rules.explanation: DDL artifacts define the database schema that must be migrated or transformed.
rules.recommendation: Review all DDL for platform-specific features (sequences, triggers, stored procedures) that need adaptation.

rules.description: IMS DL/I database calls indicate hierarchical database dependency
rules.explanation: IMS DL/I is a hierarchical database with no direct relational equivalent. Migration requires significant data model transformation.
rules.recommendation: Engage IMS specialists to map the hierarchical database to a relational or document model. This requires specialist review.
rules.upgrade_guidance: IMS DL/I hierarchical databases have no direct modern equivalent. Flag for specialist review — data model transformation is required. Do not assume a specific target database.

rules.description: VSAM datasets detected as file-based persistence
rules.detection_condition: component_type == 'FILE' and technology == 'VSAM' or component_type == 'DATASET' and technology == 'VSAM'
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact evidence_refs or detected_properties indicating VSAM
rules.explanation: VSAM datasets use mainframe-specific indexing and record organization that requires careful data migration.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all VSAM datasets, their key structures, and access patterns. Plan conversion to indexed files or database tables.
rules.upgrade_guidance: VSAM is a mainframe-specific file organization. Flag for specialist review to determine appropriate target storage.

rules.description: JCL job steps indicate batch orchestration complexity
rules.explanation: Each JCL job represents a batch process that must be re-orchestrated in the target environment.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all JCL jobs and map them to target orchestration tools (e.g., workflow schedulers).

rules.description: PROC usage in JCL indicates reusable job streams
rules.explanation: JCL PROCs are parameterized reusable job streams that add abstraction layers to batch orchestration.
rules.recommendation: Document all PROC calls, their parameter overrides, and expansion logic for target orchestration mapping.

rules.description: Multiple dataset DDs per job indicate complex I/O orchestration
rules.explanation: Each DD statement represents an input/output dataset that must be mapped to target storage and orchestrated.
rules.recommendation: Map all DD statements to target storage resources and document I/O dependencies per job.

rules.description: SORT utility usage indicates data transformation steps
rules.evidence_requirement: COBOL component with SORT verb evidence
rules.explanation: SORT operations in batch programs require mapping to target-platform sorting capabilities.
rules.recommendation: Identify all SORT operations and evaluate whether to use target-platform sort utilities or in-code sorting.

rules.description: CICS transaction calls indicate online transaction processing
rules.explanation: CICS transaction processing is a mainframe-specific online paradigm requiring significant re-architecture.
rules.recommendation: Map all CICS commands (LINK, XCTL, READ, WRITE, SEND, RECEIVE) to target-platform equivalents.
rules.upgrade_guidance: CICS is a mainframe-specific transaction processing monitor. Flag for specialist review — online architecture must be redesigned. Do not assume a specific target platform.

rules.description: BMS maps define 3270 screen layouts requiring UI re-architecture
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with category BMS_MAP or BMS
rules.explanation: BMS maps define 3270 terminal screen layouts with no direct equivalent in modern web/UI frameworks.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all BMS maps and plan a screen-by-screen UI redesign for the target platform.
rules.upgrade_guidance: BMS/3270 maps have no direct modern UI equivalent. Flag for UI specialist review to design replacement screens.

rules.description: CICS SEND/RECEIVE MAP operations indicate screen I/O coupling
rules.explanation: CICS SEND/RECEIVE MAP operations tightly couple programs to specific BMS map definitions.
rules.recommendation: Trace each SEND/RECEIVE MAP to its BMS map and plan the corresponding screen interaction.

rules.description: CICS LINK/XCTL indicates inter-program communication
rules.explanation: CICS LINK and XCTL are program-to-program communication mechanisms specific to CICS.
rules.recommendation: Document all LINK/XCTL targets and plan equivalent service calls or API invocations in the target architecture.

rules.description: CICS SYNCPOINT indicates distributed transaction coordination
rules.explanation: CICS SYNCPOINT manages distributed transaction two-phase commit, a complex pattern requiring careful target-platform mapping.
rules.recommendation: Identify all SYNCPOINT boundaries and plan distributed transaction coordination in the target architecture.

rules.description: MQ or messaging integration detected
rules.evidence_requirement: component evidence_refs indicating MQ or API
rules.explanation: Messaging integrations require understanding of message formats, queue configurations, and transactional semantics.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all MQ queues and message formats. Plan target-platform messaging equivalents.

rules.description: External system interface dependency detected
rules.explanation: External system dependencies require understanding of interface protocols, data formats, and error handling.
rules.recommendation: Document all external system interfaces, their protocols, and data exchange formats.

rules.description: Unresolved dependency target indicates missing source artifacts
rules.explanation: Unresolved dependencies point to programs, copybooks, or files whose source is not available, creating migration blind spots.
rules.recommendation: Locate and upload the missing source artifacts. Until then, these dependencies represent migration risk.

rules.description: Circular dependency detected in component graph
rules.explanation: Circular dependencies prevent straightforward migration ordering and may require architectural redesign.
rules.recommendation: Break circular dependencies before migration by introducing interfaces or intermediary components.

rules.description: Single point of dependency detected
rules.explanation: Single points of dependency concentrate risk in one component — its failure blocks many downstream components.
rules.recommendation: Identify single-point components and plan redundancy or decomposition to reduce concentration of risk.

rules.description: Security resource detected (RACF, ACF2, Top Secret references)
rules.explanation: Mainframe security resources (RACF, ACF2, Top Secret) require mapping to target-platform identity and access management.
rules.recommendation: Catalog all security resource references and plan mapping to target-platform IAM (e.g., RBAC, OAuth2).
rules.upgrade_guidance: RACF/ACF2/Top Secret are mainframe-specific security systems. Flag for security specialist review.

rules.description: JCL with SYSOUT indicates report/print output requiring target adaptation
rules.explanation: SYSOUT output in JCL represents print/report streams that need target-platform output handling.
rules.recommendation: Map SYSOUT outputs to target-platform reporting or file generation mechanisms.

rules.description: HLASM or assembler artifacts detected
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with category ASSEMBLER or HLASM
rules.explanation: HLASM/assembler code is low-level mainframe-specific code with no automated conversion path.
rules.recommendation: Engage assembler specialists. Each assembler module requires manual rewrite or wrapping. No automated conversion exists.
rules.upgrade_guidance: HLASM/assembler is end-of-life for migration purposes — no automated conversion path exists. Flag as risk requiring specialist review. Do not assume a specific target platform.

rules.description: Unsupported or detect-only artifact type reduces analysis completeness
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with support_level UNSUPPORTED or parse_status unsupported/error
rules.explanation: Artifacts that could not be fully parsed represent unknown complexity — their contents are not analyzed.
rules.recommendation: Manually review unsupported artifacts and document their contents, or provide alternative formats for analysis.

rules.description: Evidence-based components in application logic increase confidence
rules.explanation: Components with direct evidence from parsed source code increase assessment confidence.

rules.description: Inferred components reduce confidence due to indirect evidence
rules.explanation: Inferred findings rely on indirect evidence and are less reliable than directly extracted ones.
rules.recommendation: Validate inferred findings through manual review or additional source artifacts.

rules.description: COBOL programs with full parse status increase confidence
rules.explanation: Fully parsed COBOL artifacts provide reliable evidence for assessment.

rules.description: Copybook source artifacts available increase data structure confidence
rules.explanation: Available and parsed copybook sources confirm data structure definitions.

rules.description: Missing copybook artifacts referenced in code reduce confidence
rules.explanation: Copybooks referenced in code but not available as source artifacts create data structure blind spots.
rules.recommendation: Locate and upload all referenced copybook source files to resolve these gaps.

rules.description: SQL DDL artifacts available increase database confidence
rules.evidence_requirement: SQL DDL artifact with parse_status parsed
rules.explanation: Available DDL provides direct evidence of database schema structures.

rules.description: Embedded SQL without table names reduces database understanding
rules.detection_condition: component_type == 'TABLE' and detected_properties.tables not present or empty
rules.evidence_requirement: SQL component without table names extracted
rules.explanation: When embedded SQL table names cannot be extracted, database dependency mapping is incomplete.
rules.recommendation: Review the SQL statements manually to identify table references that the parser could not extract.

rules.description: JCL artifacts with full parse status increase batch confidence
rules.explanation: Fully parsed JCL artifacts provide reliable evidence for batch orchestration assessment.

rules.description: Missing JCL artifacts reduce batch confidence
rules.explanation: If no JCL is available, batch orchestration cannot be assessed — this does not mean there is no batch processing.
rules.recommendation: Locate and upload all JCL files for the application to enable batch orchestration assessment.

rules.description: BMS map artifacts available increase online UI confidence
rules.evidence_requirement: BMS map artifact with parse_status parsed
rules.explanation: Available BMS maps provide direct evidence of online screen layouts.

rules.description: Unresolved dependency targets reduce integration confidence
rules.explanation: Each unresolved dependency means a referenced component has no source, creating integration analysis gaps.
rules.recommendation: Resolve unresolved dependencies by uploading missing source artifacts.

rules.description: Dependency discovery completed increases integration confidence
rules.explanation: Completed dependency discovery provides evidence of inter-component relationships.

rules.description: No security artifacts found reduces security confidence
rules.explanation: Absence of security evidence does not mean the application has no security — it means we cannot assess it.
rules.recommendation: Provide security configuration files, RACF rule definitions, or documentation to enable security assessment.

rules.description: Unsupported artifact types reduce overall assessment confidence
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with support_level UNSUPPORTED or parse_status unsupported/error
rules.explanation: Unsupported artifacts contain unanalyzed content — missing evidence reduces assessment confidence.
rules.recommendation: Provide alternative formats or manual documentation for unsupported artifacts.

rules.description: Detect-only parser capability reduces confidence for those artifacts
rules.explanation: Detect-only parsing confirms file type but does not extract internal structure, limiting analysis depth.
rules.recommendation: Consider providing parsed or annotated versions of detect-only artifacts.

rules.description: Human-validated findings increase confidence
rules.explanation: Human review of machine-generated findings increases the reliability of assessment conclusions.
rules.recommendation: Conduct periodic human review of automated findings, especially for high-severity results.

rules.description: Application owner documented increases readiness
rules.explanation: A documented application owner indicates organizational readiness for migration planning.

rules.description: Missing application owner reduces readiness
rules.explanation: Without a known owner, migration planning cannot proceed for this application.
rules.recommendation: Assign an application owner before proceeding with detailed migration planning.

rules.description: All referenced copybooks available increases data readiness
rules.evidence_requirement: all copybook components have non-Unknown evidence_class
rules.explanation: Complete copybook availability means data structures are fully visible for migration planning.

rules.description: Missing copybooks reduce data structure readiness
rules.explanation: Missing copybooks mean data structure definitions are incomplete, blocking migration planning.
rules.recommendation: Locate and upload all missing copybook files before proceeding.

rules.description: DDL available increases database readiness
rules.explanation: Available DDL provides the schema understanding needed for database migration planning.

rules.description: Missing DDL reduces database readiness
rules.evidence_requirement: TABLE components exist but no SQL_DDL artifacts
rules.explanation: Programs embed SQL but no DDL is available — schema cannot be fully understood.
rules.recommendation: Obtain DDL scripts for all referenced databases to complete schema understanding.

rules.description: JCL available increases batch readiness
rules.explanation: Available and parsed JCL provides batch job understanding for orchestration planning.

rules.description: BMS maps available increases online UI readiness
rules.explanation: Available BMS maps provide screen layout understanding for UI migration planning.

rules.description: Dependency graph completed increases integration readiness
rules.explanation: A completed dependency graph provides visibility into inter-component relationships needed for migration planning.

rules.description: Unresolved dependencies reduce integration readiness
rules.explanation: Unresolved dependencies represent unknown integration points that block migration planning.
rules.recommendation: Resolve all unresolved dependencies before proceeding with detailed migration planning.

rules.description: No security documentation reduces security readiness
rules.explanation: Without security evidence, security controls cannot be assessed or planned for migration.
rules.recommendation: Provide security configuration, access control documentation, or compliance requirements.

rules.description: Unsupported artifacts reduce operational readiness
rules.evidence_requirement: artifact with support_level UNSUPPORTED or parse_status unsupported/error
rules.explanation: Unsupported artifacts represent unknown operational characteristics that block readiness.
rules.recommendation: Provide alternative formats or manual documentation for unsupported artifacts.

rules.description: Business domain documented increases operational readiness
rules.explanation: Documented business domain provides context for operational requirements understanding.

rules.description: Technology stack documented increases operational readiness
rules.explanation: Documented technology stack provides baseline understanding for target platform planning.
